options: A free Microsoft Sysinternals tool, not installed by default, that provides much deeper system-activity logging than native Windows auditing
A built-in Windows feature enabled automatically on every version of Windows
A paid third-party antivirus product
A replacement for the Security log that disables default Windows auditing
questions.explain: Sysmon (System Monitor) is a free Sysinternals tool that someone must deliberately download and install as a service plus driver; it is not on by default.

questions.q: What does Sysmon's Event ID 1 (Process Create) capture that native Windows auditing typically doesn't include by default?
options: The full command line a process was launched with, plus its hash and parent process
The exact amount of RAM the process used
The user's typed password
The physical location of the server
questions.explain: Event ID 1 logs the full command line, hash, and parent process — exactly the detail that reveals whether a process like powershell.exe was invoked normally or with obfuscated arguments.

questions.q: What does Sysmon Event ID 3 record?
options: A network connection initiated by a process, including source/destination IP and port
A user account being created
A file's creation timestamp being changed
A successful logon
questions.explain: Event ID 3 turns 'something reached the internet' into 'this specific process reached this specific address' by logging the connection details.

questions.q: Where does Sysmon write its events in Event Viewer?
options: Applications and Services Logs > Microsoft > Windows > Sysmon > Operational
Directly into the Security log, replacing native audit events
Into the System log only
Sysmon does not use Event Viewer at all
questions.explain: Sysmon writes to its own dedicated operational log, separate from the Security log covered in Lessons 9 and 10.

questions.q: Why do most real Sysmon deployments start from a published community configuration (such as SwiftOnSecurity's) rather than running Sysmon unconfigured?
options: Without include/exclude filtering, Sysmon can generate an overwhelming volume of events
Sysmon refuses to run without a config file
Community configs are required by Microsoft licensing
Unconfigured Sysmon logs nothing at all
questions.explain: The XML configuration file defines what Sysmon includes or excludes from logging — essential for managing event volume in a real environment.
